item_name: Lappalainen et al. 2024 FlyVis (Nature) and later works that retrain or reuse FlyVis for non-flow tasks

full_text_checked: P1: bioRxiv preprint full text read via HTML (main text plus Methods to the reference list; the part after char 200000 was not read). Nature final version and PMC were blocked (paywall redirect / bot check), so final-version wording is not verified; numbers are taken from the preprint plus the local code config (flyvis/config/task/task.yaml, scheduler/scheduler.yaml, datasets/sintel.py). F1: v1 HTML read through a summary; v2 PDF text extracted locally (11 pages), with abstract, sections 5.1-5.4 and 7.1 and the figures listing controls read directly. F2: GitHub README only. F3, F4, F5: arXiv/bioRxiv HTML full text via summary (F4 truncated in Appendix E). F6: paywalled; only a search snippet was seen. T1: abstract-level only.
task_and_output: P1: dense optic-flow regression. A decoder reads instantaneous activity of 34 output cell types (medulla and downstream) and outputs a 2D flow vector per hexal on the 721-column lattice; loss is squared error (config 'l2norm'). Code also supports a 'depth' task in MultiTaskSintel, but the paper reports only flow and states that motion detection is one of many computations of the visual system (no other task tested). F1: one-shot hatch (texture) matching in architectural drawings, nearest legend class by cosine similarity on a 1,368-d descriptor (57 non-input cell types x 3 statistics x 8 prescribed drift trajectories). v2 adds wall segmentation per column (IoU/AP). F2: frame-wise detection of small drones (5-60 px); hit@25 and AUC from a spatial readout of FlyVis activity. F3: MovingEdge direction decoding (2D direction vector) using a linear decoder. F4: no new task; stress tests of mechanistic claims (reverse-phi, sawtooth, adversarial margins, attribution, circuits). F5: no new task; RSA/CKA of peak central-cell voltages for 65 cell types on moving edges. F6: linear decoding of 6-way motion direction from a frozen checkpoint with apparent scale held out [uncertain]. No reused work outputs a centroid, box, presence score or target-conditioned localization in tracking.
data_and_independent_videos: P1: MPI Sintel training sequences (grayscale, 1024x436 px, 24 fps), 19-frame clips, random temporal crops and vertical splits (3), center crop 0.7. Train/validation split by scene: subsamples of one scene are not shared between train and validation. Evaluation of biology uses synthetic stimuli (flashes, moving edges, gratings) compared with 26 published studies. F1: synthetic 'smell_v3' benchmark on CubiCasa5K wall geometry with procedural hatches; TRAIN/DEV/TEST 400 sheets each; DEV has 257 source-plan clusters; v2 adds a preregistered held-out split opened once and a closed set of 14 real production sheets. F2: ETH Zurich drone-tracking-datasets, 21 videos from 4 datasets; dev clips used for tuning and 84 test clips run once, but dev and test come from the same 21 videos (author caveat), so this is not an unseen-video test. F3: MovingEdge stimuli (12 stimuli, 269 frames). F5: MovingEdge stimuli at 19 deg/s, 12 or 24 conditions. No work uses BDD100K or real driving-type videos with moving camera at 30 Hz.
target_size_and_input_resolution: P1: 721 hexagonal photoreceptor columns (31 columns across), each the box average of a 13x13 px patch, 13 px spacing (config boxfilter kernel 13, extent 15); column spacing about 5.8 deg in the model's biological interpretation; single-column receptive fields for Mi1/Mi4/Mi9/Tm1/Tm2/Tm9/CT1 and about two columns (11.6 deg) for Tm3/Tm4. Network: 45,669 neurons, 1,513,231 connections, 64 cell types in the abstract (65 counting CT1 compartments separately). No objects or targets defined. F1: 64x64 grayscale patches resized to the eye frame on 721 columns (a 1,951-column 'big eye' variant was also tested); a texture fills the region, so there is no small target. F2: drones of 5-60 px in full frames; mapping to hexals is not reported. Our crops (targets about 9.4 x 12.1 lattice steps) are larger in lattice units than any FlyVis-trained structure except full-field flow.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: P1: Sintel at 24 fps, resampled and flow interpolated to the integration step dt = 0.02 s (50 Hz; config task.dataset.dt and scheduler dt 0.02); the preprint says steps shorter than 20 ms did not improve performance or tuning; 500 ms grey initialisation; synthetic stimuli integrated at 5-10 ms. Sintel contains strong camera and object motion (rendered film). F1: prescribed drift, 12 frames at 20 ms, 4 directions x 2 speeds, first 4 frames discarded; no camera. F2: real video from static multi-camera rigs (frame rate not retrieved). F3/F5: synthetic moving edges, no camera motion.
detector_and_exemplar: P1: no detector, no exemplar. F1: exemplar = 4 legend windows per class on the same sheet (one-shot per sheet); features standardised per sheet transductively; nearest-class matching; v1 has no abstention, v2 adds an abstention threshold fixed on development data. F2: no external detector; FlyVis plus a spatio-temporal readout is the detector, compared with MOG2, frame difference and an EMD (Reichardt) detector. F3-F6: no detector or exemplar.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: P1: 734 free parameters: 65 resting potentials + 65 membrane time constants (one per cell type) + 604 non-negative synapse scaling factors (one per cell-type pair); synapse counts (2,355 types) and signs (604) are fixed from the connectome. Decoder (DecoderGAVP: 5x5 conv, 34 -> 8 channels, batch norm, softplus, dropout 0.5, then a conv to 3 channels, the third as shared normalisation) is trained jointly. Loss: L2 on flow; BPTT, Adam, lr 5e-5 -> 5e-6 in 10 steps, batch 4, about 250,000 iterations, checkpoint selected by validation EPE; augmentation: hex-axis flips, six-fold rotations, contrast std 0.2, brightness std 0.1, Gaussian noise 0.08. F1: FlyVis core frozen (checkpoint 001 in v1); no weights updated on hatch labels; v2 also trains readouts and CNN decoders on top for segmentation (fly readout about 1.9k parameters; fly + conv decoder about 27k). F2: 10 of the 50 pretrained networks, apparently used without retraining [uncertain]. F3: 734 core parameters trained for 5-10 update steps plus a linear decoder (MSE, Adam 1e-3), on intact or rewired graphs. F4/F5: pretrained ensemble, no training except the comparison CNNs in F4 (8,161 / 50,002 / 988,418 parameters, 5 seeds). No work fine-tunes the FlyVis core for an object, tracking or target-conditioned task with a matched comparison against a frozen core.
controls_seeds_splits: P1: ensemble of 50 models with the same connectome and task (main analyses on the 10 best; the 10 worst in Extended Data Fig. 4); random-parameter DMNs with only the decoder trained (Extended Data Fig. 3); unconstrained CNNs (414,666 parameters, 5 models) as a lower bound on task error; synthetic sparse versus dense connectomes (Extended Data Fig. 9). No shuffled or degree-preserving fly-connectome control in the visible text. F1 v2: (a) receptors-only descriptor from the same moving 721-receptor signal; (b) degree-preserving rewiring, type-pair and sign-preserving rewiring, and Erdos-Renyi graphs, 3 rewiring seeds each, with invariants verified; (c) positive control silencing R7/R8; (d) T4/T5 knockout; (e) moving versus still frame; (f) task-trained CNNs 1,934-365,921 parameters, 3 sizes x 3 seeds; (g) frozen large encoders (DINOv2/v3, SigLIP 2, PE-core); bootstrap over source-plan clusters (5,000 resamples); preregistered held-out split opened once. Caveat: the rewired nulls keep parameters fitted to the intact graph, so they test 'does breaking a trained circuit hurt', not 'is the topology better when trained'. F2: raw-input control with the same readout; a shuffled-connectome control was attempted but rejected because it diverged without retraining; 10 networks. F3: naive random graph and degree-preserving rewiring (5 samples, 250,000 swaps), seeds {0,1,2}, checkpoint versus shared from-scratch initialisation. F4: task-matched causal CNNs at 3 sizes, 5 seeds. F5: sign-preserving shuffles of the 734 parameters (n = 50, stability-filtered) and untrained networks at the prior.
metrics_and_numbers: P1 (preprint): ensemble median FRI predicts ON/OFF preference for 31/31 cell types (p = 4.7e-10), best model 29/31; 12 of 19 cell types with asymmetric multicolumnar inputs predicted motion-selective; higher task performance predicts T4/T5 DSI better (p = 5.6e-6, Wald); task-optimised versus random DMNs DSI p = 2e-11, FRI p = 5.3e-5 (Extended Data Fig. 5). Task EPE (Extended Data Fig. 3): task-optimised DMNs 5.1-5.5 a.u., random DMNs with trained decoder about 5.7, unconstrained CNNs 4.5-4.6. Sparse synthetic networks at 10% connectivity: median Pearson r 0.856 (Extended Data Fig. 9). F1 v1 (Table 2, 400 DEV sheets): fly + drift 0.857 area-weighted accuracy; receptors only 0.891; Gabor 0.802; big eye 0.888; static mask 0.838 vs moving 0.857; task-trained CNN with 5,888 parameters 0.959 (Table 4, 3 seeds). F1 v2: held-out split (Table 3) fly 0.835, receptors only 0.894, receptors lead by +0.059 [0.043, 0.075], trained networks 0.971-0.980 (+0.136 to +0.144); abstention at a dev-fixed threshold: fly answers 75.5% at 0.913 [0.897, 0.927] accuracy (lower bound just under the 0.90 target), receptors only 88.7% at 0.921 [0.906, 0.936], trained networks decline nothing (Section 5.4). Rewiring (Section 7.1, DEV): 0.857 -> 0.539 degree-preserving (+0.318 [0.296, 0.339]), 0.586 type/sign-preserving (+0.271), 0.500 Erdos-Renyi (+0.356); R7/R8 silencing costs 0.092 [0.079, 0.104]; segmentation null 0.483 -> 0.089 IoU. Fly front end in front of a conv decoder 0.925 AP versus the same CNN on receptors without the circuit 0.919 AP (Figure 8); T4/T5 silencing leaves both tasks intact (abstract). Real sheets: fly 0.505 AP versus 0.415 for a 200x larger CNN (Table 5, 14 sheets). F2 (README): hit@25 EMD+ST 77.4% (AUC 0.886), MOG2 75.3% (0.827), flyvis+ST 71.1% (0.880), -6.3 points vs EMD+ST [-10.7; -2.3], raw-input control 68.8%, frame difference 69.7%; flyvis about 31 ms/frame vs about 11 ms. F3 (Table 2): with checkpoint initialisation the connectome looks better (delta loss 0.184 at 5 steps), but with shared from-scratch initialisation and degree-preserving nulls the gaps vanish (delta loss -0.0018 to 0.0017). F4: T4/T5 output silencing reduces the optic-flow behaviour to at most 2 of 8 clips in 40/50 models; 0/50 reproduce the sawtooth response; adversarial margin 0.21-0.27 vs 0.13-0.25 contrast for CNNs. F5: trained CC vs shuffled RSA r = 0.686 (Exp 1), 0.846 (Exp 2); untrained CC vs shuffled r = 0.260 (p = 0.041, not Bonferroni-significant).
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: P1 yes (scene-held-out Sintel validation, flow only); F1 not videos (held-out drawing split, yes for held-out sheets); F2 no (dev and test from the same 21 videos); F3-F5 not applicable. Target absence: not reported in P1, F2-F5; F1 v2 tests abstention (declining low-confidence regions), not target absence. Similar distractors: not reported in any (F1 has competing legend classes, which is the nearest analogue). Occlusion: not reported. Night or low light: not reported (P1 uses contrast/brightness augmentation and noise only). Sequential operation on own predictions: not reported in any work; P1 is open-loop on fixed clips, F2 is per-frame detection without tracking feedback.
mechanism_summary: Published mechanism (P1): a recurrent graded-potential network with the fixed optic-lobe connectome on 721 hexagonal columns; only 734 cell-type-shared parameters (time constants, resting potentials, synapse-type scales) are fitted with a spatial conv decoder on optic flow from Sintel at dt 20 ms; the 50-model ensemble varies in how well it predicts physiology, and better task performance goes with better T4/T5 direction tuning. The task constrains which solution the connectome reaches; the connectome alone does not fix dynamics (supported independently by T1 theory and by F3/F4). Published reuse: all forward works reuse the motion-trained ensemble frozen (F1, F2, F4, F5, F6) or retrain the 734 parameters only for direction decoding (F3). Common finding: the frozen circuit transfers somewhat, but a readout on the same receptor input (F1 receptors-only, F2 raw input + readout, and F2 EMD hand-built motion) equals or beats it, and silencing T4/T5 does not hurt the non-flow task (F1). Breaking the wiring of a fitted model hurts (F1 rewiring), which shows that the fitted parameters depend on the graph, not that the graph helps a new task. Proposed modification (ours, not published): use FlyVis as a target-conditioned localizer with refusal, which requires a new readout and possibly core retraining; no published evidence that core retraining for an object task helps beyond input features.
transfer_limits: 1) Task gap: FlyVis was trained only on dense optic flow; no published work trained or validated it for object identity, re-identification among similar neighbours, or target absence; F1 is texture matching, F2 is detection with a static camera and the fly loses to a Reichardt baseline and adds only 2.3 points over raw input. 2) Temporal gap: trained at dt 20 ms (50 Hz) with 24 fps frames interpolated; at our 30 Hz each frame step is a 33 ms displacement, so either interpolate to 50 Hz (as in training) or accept a rate mismatch; P1 shows nothing about 30 Hz. 3) Spatial gap: 721 grey hexals from 13x13 box averages; targets of about 9x12 lattice steps occupy roughly 100 columns, but the useful motion cells (T4/T5) integrate over 1-2 columns, so identity cues of similar neighbours (colour, fine texture) are largely removed by the grey box filter; F1 shows a 1,951-column eye helps (0.888 vs 0.857). 4) Ego-motion of the moving, rescaling crop: Sintel has camera motion, but crop rescaling changes apparent speed and scale; F6 reports only range-limited scale stability of direction codes [uncertain]. 5) Refusal: none of the works output a calibrated presence score; F1 v2 abstention on a frozen descriptor nearly misses its 0.90 guarantee on held-out data (0.913, lower bound 0.897), consistent with our observation that high confidence poorly marks useful corrections (7 of 37). 6) Environment: no work uses a detector+tracker pipeline (YOLO/ByteTrack/MASA); the fly signal must beat a matched readout on the same 721 receptors (receptors-only) and the no-FlyVis variant B, not only stock FlyVis. 7) Compute: 31 ms/frame per crop in F2; batching many tracks at 12 GB is feasible but must be measured.
research_questions_addressed: Q2 (direct evidence, strongest): F1 gives the published procedure that separates representation from readout on identical observations: receptors-only descriptor built from the same moving 721-receptor signal, matched graph nulls, T4/T5 knockout, and the fly front end in front of a conv decoder versus the same decoder on receptors; outcome: the circuit adds nothing beyond its own retina. P1 random-parameter DMNs with trained decoder (EPE about 5.7 vs 5.1-5.5) is the stock version of a 'frozen random core' control. F3 shows that apparent topology benefits vanish under shared initialisation and degree-preserving nulls. Q5 (design analogy and caution): the minimal control set for our C/D comparisons should include receptors-only with the same readout and capacity, a degree-preserving rewired FlyVis retrained under the same budget (rewiring without retraining is not a fair null, F2 diverged, F1 conflates), and the 50-model ensemble spread. Q3 (caution): FlyVis integrates at 20 ms on interpolated 24 fps input; no evidence on 30 Hz, moving crops, or object scale. Q4 (caution): F1 v2 is the only abstention result and shows threshold transfer barely holds for the frozen fly descriptor. Q1 (no direct evidence): no FlyVis work selects one of two similar targets or refuses on absence.
candidate_node_change: Node: readout plus input of the fly eye, tested against the receptor (input) node. Concrete change suggested by F1: build the target-conditioned localizer readout over the concatenation of (a) FlyVis output-type activity and (b) the raw 721 photoreceptor time series of the same moving crop, with an exemplar-similarity map and a refusal head, and treat the FlyVis branch as useful only if removing it hurts. Controls on identical cached observations and history: (1) without FlyVis: receptors-only branch with the same readout and parameter count (this is a stronger and more specific control than B, because it keeps the exact eye input and motion); (2) stock FlyVis: frozen flow/0000 core with the same readout (variant C); (3) optional: core trained (D) and a degree-preserving rewired core retrained with the same budget, to separate topology from extra trainable parameters (F3). Minimal check: on the existing Z13 dev observations, paired comparison by video of useful-centre rate and refusal precision at a fixed coverage (for example top 1% and 10% confidence) for receptors-only versus receptors+FlyVis, 3 seeds, bootstrap over videos; then T4/T5 silencing in the FlyVis branch as a mechanism check. Stop condition: if receptors+FlyVis minus receptors-only has a 95% CI that includes 0 or is negative on useful-centre rate and on refusal precision, stop attributing the localizer to FlyVis (record as a readout/tracker result, AGENTS rule 6.16), and do not proceed to HOTA with MASA; also stop if T4/T5 silencing does not change the outcome (the motion pathway is not used). Proceed to HOTA only if the paired gain is positive with CI above 0 and refusal calibration holds on held-out val videos.
strongest_objection: Every published reuse of FlyVis outside optic flow uses a frozen motion-trained model and finds that a readout on the same receptor input matches or beats the circuit (F1: 0.894 vs 0.835 held out; F2: the fly loses to a hand-built EMD and adds 2.3 points over raw input; F1: T4/T5 knockout harmless; conv decoder on receptors 0.919 vs fly+decoder 0.925 AP). The evidence that 'wiring is load-bearing' (F1 rewiring) only shows that a fitted model breaks when its graph is scrambled, not that the connectome helps a new task. None of these works fine-tune the core for an object-level task, so there is neither positive nor negative published evidence for our D variant; all reuse sources are single-author preprints or a draft from 2026, unreplicated. P1 itself makes claims only about motion physiology, not about object identity, so it cannot justify FlyVis as a re-identification module among similar neighbours.
evidence_strength: P1: peer-reviewed (Nature 2024), code and 50-model ensemble public and verified locally (flyvis 1.2.0 config: dt 0.02, batch 4, 250,000 iterations, augmentation as stated); strong for the motion-physiology claim, not applicable to object tasks. F1: single-author arXiv preprint (2 versions within 2 days), preregistered held-out split and matched nulls, code/data not fully released; moderate for the 'circuit adds nothing beyond receptors' finding in texture matching, weak for transfer to tracking. F2: unpublished draft on GitHub, same-video dev/test; weak. F3, F4, F5: single-author or two-author preprints, 2026, unreplicated; weak to moderate. F6: peer-reviewed but full text not accessed [uncertain]. Overall for our decision: moderate evidence that frozen FlyVis features are not better than its own receptor input for non-flow tasks; no evidence either way for retraining the core for object re-identification with refusal.
